subject: Clarify metered bundle structuring + distributor uplift for private offer
messages:
From: Elena Morozova <elena.m@cloudscale.io>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on private offer metered bundle and distributor uplift

Sergio — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a couple of follow-ups before we can move to a PO:

1) We want the private offer to be metered (token-based) but sold as a bundle (search + embeddings + rerank). How do you recommend structuring SKUs so our distributor (DataPartners Inc.) can invoice correctly and we can maintain a single monthly commitment?

2) Our channel team is asking for a +6% distributor uplift on top of list price. Will that be applied as a gross list add-on (i.e., vendor-facing margin) or as a passback on invoice credits? We need to model cash flow for audits.

3) Any constraints on using usage discounts that phase-in by tier (0-10M tokens: 10% off; 10M-50M: 20%) with a seat-based minimum? Procurement prefers clear ceilings and passthroughs.

Appreciate any examples or a short proposal.

—Elena
Director, Cloud Procurement
CloudScale Analytics

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Morozova <elena.m@cloudscale.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private offer metered bundle and distributor uplift

Thanks Elena — looping in Ben from GTM and Soojin from Partnerships to propose an ops-safe structure. High level answers up front:

- We can create three consumable SKUs (search_tokens, embed_tokens, rerank_tokens) and publish a composite bundle SKU that ties them together on the private offer. The private offer enforces a single committed monthly spend while metering usage across the underlying SKUs.

- Distributor uplift can be handled two ways (see below). For CloudScale your team prefers cashflow clarity, so we recommend a passback model: Redwood invoices CloudScale at net list, DataPartners invoices you including their uplift, and you organize a passback or rebate to reconcile. This gives clear ledger entries for audits.

- Tiered usage discounts are supported. We advise capping the effective discount at an aggregated ceiling to avoid unexpected negative unit economics (we can model on the attached). Seat minimums can be implemented as a separate SKU (seat_base) that must be purchased to enable the metered bundle.

Ben — can you draft a short proposal (1 page + attachments) with enumeration of SKUs, sample invoice flows for both uplift models, and a simple cost waterfall? Soojin — any channel/contract constraints we should flag for Elena?

Thanks,
Sergio
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com, Elena Morozova <elena.m@cloudscale.io>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private offer metered bundle and distributor uplift

Elena — attached is a concise example pack (redwood_sku_proposal_v3.xlsx) and a channel fee workback (channel_fee_workback_v2.pdf). TL;DR for modeling: 

Proposed structure (ops-friendly):
- SKU set: RWI-BUNDLE-COMMIT (composite) -> underlying metered SKUs: RWI-SEARCH-TOK, RWI-EMBED-TOK, RWI-RERANK-TOK
- Seat base: RWI-SEAT-MIN (monthly fixed), optional but recommended to guarantee minimum MRR and invoice shape
- Private offer: committed monthly spend applied to composite; any overage billed against underlying metered SKUs at published private-offer rates

Two channel handling options (pros/cons):
A) Distributor uplift baked into reseller price (simple, but obscures vendor invoice and complicates Redwood reconciliation if uplift varies).
B) Distributor uplift as passback / rebate (preferred for audit) — Redwood invoices CloudScale at net private-offer rates; DataPartners invoices CloudScale including +6%. At month end, either CloudScale remits uplift to DataPartners directly or we calculate a rebate credit on CloudScale's subscription (your choice).

Example waterfall (see spreadsheet):
- List price per token -> private-offer discount -> effective net price -> distributor uplift (+6%) -> customer billed amount.

We included sample line items and a worked example at 12M tokens/month with a tiered discount cadence. Notes: if uplift is externalized (passback), accounting treats it as a third-party reseller fee and won't change Redwood's revenue recognition. If uplift is internalized (baked into price) Redwood's invoiced revenue will be higher and revenue shares must be reconciled with distributor contracts.

Operational asks from our side:
- Confirm whether you prefer distributor to invoice directly (DataPartners -> CloudScale) or have Redwood include distributor uplift on a consolidated invoice and remit to DataPartners.
- Confirm seat_min threshold if you want that enforced.

I'll be at the channel sync next week; happy to walk through the spreadsheet live.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morozova <elena.m@cloudscale.io>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.io>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private offer metered bundle and distributor uplift

Thanks Ben — that was helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and finance: 

- For auditability we strongly prefer option B (passback/rebate). Can you confirm what artifacts Redwood can provide monthly for reconciliation? We need: invoice-level usage export, SKU mappings, and the private-offer rate table.

- For the seat_min: proposing a 3-seat minimum at $1,500/mo as a floor. Can Redwood enforce that as a required add-on SKU rather than a contractual separate line? Procurement wants the invoice to show it as a billed SKU.

- Regarding tiered discounts: can we request an annual true-up process if aggregated usage crosses higher tiers mid-year? Finance wants to avoid retroactive credits unless there's a simple True-up schedule.

If you can confirm the artifacts and whether Redwood will put seat_min as a billed SKU, we can draft the PO template and loop in DataPartners to align invoicing.

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Elena Morozova <elena.m@cloudscale.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private offer metered bundle and distributor uplift

Elena — great, thanks for the specifics. Quick confirmations and next steps:

- Artifacts: we will provide a monthly usage CSV export (token granularity by SKU), a SKU mapping PDF (human-readable), and the private-offer rate table (versioned CSV). We'll attach the first set to the HubSpot deal and grant DataPartners read access to the reconciliation Drive folder.

- Seat minimum: yes, we can implement RWI-SEAT-MIN as a billed SKU on the private offer (will appear as a recurring line item). Engineering/ops have to approve SKU enforcement but this is standard; I'll mark it as an ops dependency in the checklist.

- True-up: we support an annual true-up cadence with a simple threshold rule (aggregate usage > next tier by X% triggers true-up). We'll add a template clause to the PO language; legal is comfortable with the standard form we use with other resellers.

Action items:
1) Ben to share the finalized spreadsheet with modeled scenarios and one-pager (by Mon 6/21).
2) Soojin to coordinate with DataPartners on invoicing preference and grant folder access.
3) Sergio to add seat SKU enforcement request to ops ticket and push for a PO template with true-up clause.

I'll draft a short email to DataPartners cc'ing Procurement once Ben's materials are in place. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min ops alignment next week.

Thanks — will keep this thread as the single source of record.

Sergio Alvarez
